findings.title: Superfluous name guard before setFormValue — the condition is misleading
findings.description: In _handleClick (hx-button.ts line 223-225), the form submission path checks 'this.name !== undefined && this.value !== undefined' before calling this._internals.setFormValue(this.value). ElementInternals.setFormValue() does not require a name — the form data key is determined by the element's HTML name attribute, which ElementInternals reads automatically from the form-associated element. The guard on this.name does not prevent incorrect behavior, but it creates the false impression that name is required for setFormValue to work. If a button has value but no name attribute, setFormValue is still called correctly without this guard. The guard only prevents setFormValue when both name AND value are missing, but the value-only case should also call setFormValue.
findings.recommendation: Simplify to: if (this.value !== undefined) { this._internals.setFormValue(this.value); }. Or document explicitly why name is checked if there is a design intent here.

findings.title: Primary variant hover reassigns --hx-button-bg to same value as default — filter is sole hover signal
findings.description: In hx-button.styles.ts lines 141-143, the .button--primary:hover rule sets --hx-button-bg: var(--hx-button-hover-bg, var(--hx-color-primary-500)), which is identical to the default primary value (--hx-color-primary-500). The hover visual change for primary buttons comes entirely from filter: brightness(0.9) defined on .button:hover. This is not broken, but is architecturally inconsistent: all other hover variants (secondary, tertiary, danger, ghost, outline) change --hx-button-bg to a different color, while primary relies on filter. The :host([inverted]) .button:hover then resets filter: none, which means inverted primary buttons lose their hover indication entirely (filter removed but --hx-button-bg unchanged from default).
findings.recommendation: Either: (1) Change primary hover to use a distinct color like var(--hx-color-primary-600) so the pattern is consistent with other variants; or (2) explicitly document in a comment that primary hover is filter-based. Also verify inverted primary button has a hover state when filter is reset.

findings.title: hx-size attribute name deviates from HTML attribute naming conventions
findings.description: The size property is exposed as the hx-size HTML attribute (attribute: 'hx-size' in @property decorator), while all other properties use plain attribute names (variant, disabled, loading, type, href, target, full, inverted). This inconsistency requires consumers to write <hx-button hx-size='sm'> rather than <hx-button size='sm'>, breaking the principle of least surprise. The name attribute (a standard HTML attribute) is used directly without prefix. This was documented as P3-01 in the prior audit and flagged for the next major version.
findings.currentCode:
@property({ type: String, reflect: true, attribute: 'hx-size' })
size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md';
findings.recommendation: Normalize to plain 'size' attribute in the next major version. The prior audit notes this would be a breaking change. Document the planned normalization in a @deprecated-style note on the property.

findings.title: Base .button rule retains last-resort hex fallbacks bypassing token cascade
findings.description: Lines 32-33 of hx-button.styles.ts contain hardcoded hex fallbacks in the base .button rule: background-color: var(--hx-button-bg, var(--hx-color-primary-500, #2563eb)) and color: var(--hx-button-color, var(--hx-color-neutral-0, #ffffff)). Per AUDIT.md, this is intentional ('The base .button rule retains its last-resort hex fallback for the unthemed case'). However, if the design system's primary color changes from #2563eb, unthemed deployments will silently render the old color. This is a maintenance hazard rather than an active bug.
findings.recommendation: Accept as-is if unthemed rendering is a deliberate design requirement. If not, remove the hex terminal fallbacks so token misconfiguration fails visibly rather than silently.

findings.title: Variant validation spreads read-only tuple unnecessarily
findings.description: In updated() (hx-button.ts line 172), the valid variants tuple is spread into a new string array: const validVariants: string[] = [...HelixButton._VALID_VARIANTS]. This spread is unnecessary — the .includes() check only needs the tuple to be iterable. The spread creates a new array allocation on every update cycle where variant changes.
findings.recommendation: Use: if (!(HelixButton._VALID_VARIANTS as readonly string[]).includes(this.variant)) { ... } to avoid the allocation. Or cast the variant type: (HelixButton._VALID_VARIANTS as readonly string[]).includes(this.variant).

positiveFindingsPreserve.detail: Zero 'any' types throughout the component, library, and test file. All union types correctly defined (variant, size, type). No @ts-ignore or non-null assertions (!). Proper use of 'override' keyword on lifecycle methods.

Correct decorator usage (@customElement, @property). TemplateResult return types on _renderSpinner and _renderInner. classMap for dynamic classes. ifDefined for optional attributes. nothing used correctly throughout for ARIA attribute omission. static override styles array pattern. Proper separation of render helpers.

P0-01 (WCAG 4.1.2 icon-only accessible name) is fully resolved. The mixin exposes ariaLabel and ariaLabelledBy as reactive properties that are forwarded to inner elements. Both button and anchor branches forward aria-label=${this.ariaLabel ?? nothing}.

Correct use of static formAssociated = true, attachInternals(), requestSubmit() for submit, form.reset() for reset, and formDisabledCallback. Tests cover formAssociated, form getter, submit, reset, and setFormValue paths.
rel='noopener noreferrer' automatically applied when target='_blank'. href correctly removed for both disabled and loading states, preventing navigation bypass via middle-click or ctrl-click.

90+ tests across 16 test groups: Rendering, variant, size, disabled, type, loading, combined states, href mode, events, keyboard, slots, CSS parts, form, form association, form validation, lifecycle, slot handler, programmatic changes, accessibility (axe-core). axe-core integrated for all variants.

Three-tier cascade implemented: --hx-button-* component tokens with --hx-color-* semantic fallbacks. Private CSS custom properties (--hx-button-hover-bg as consumer override hook). Token naming follows --hx- prefix convention consistently.

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) disables spinner animation and transitions. @media (forced-colors: active) provides Windows High Contrast Mode support using system colors (ButtonFace, ButtonText, GrayText, Highlight). Opacity reset in HCM prevents stacking with forced-colors rendering.
Correctly declared at module scope, enabling TypeScript type inference for querySelector('hx-button').
